lists.title: Metropolitan Free Hospital: donations and subscriptions announced at the anniversary festival
lists.purpose: Gratuitous relief of the sick poor of all nations, without letter of introduction, at 8 Devonshire Square, Bishopsgate Street.
lists.notes: Advertisement printed 16 April 1851. Gifts announced at the hospital’s anniversary festival at the London Tavern, Bishopsgate Street, on Wednesday 2 April 1851, David Salomons, Esq., Alderman, in the chair. Entries marked “a” in the list are annual subscriptions (entered with the role subscriber); the rest are donations. The notice addresses Jewish readers: a Hebrew visitor had said the hospital “might almost be called the Jews’ Hospital”, as it relieved about 5,000 cases a year among the Jewish poor, and the Committee appealed to “the wealthy members of the Hebrew persuasion”. A donation of ten guineas made the donor a Life Governor; an annual guinea, a Governor. 322 entries totalling £1,309 12s. 1d. as transcribed; no total is printed. Most donors are not Jewish.

lists.title: Congregation of Portsmouth: donations for altering the synagogue entrance and building alms houses
lists.purpose: The fund for alteration of the entrance of the synagogue, building of alms houses, etc.
lists.notes: Donations acknowledged by the Committee, after an “amount of subscriptions already advertised” of £501 5s. (not counted here). 11 entries totalling £17 0s. 6d. as transcribed. The congregation is linked to the Portsea Hebrew Congregation record (its synagogue was in Portsea).
